scholarships.title: International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program)
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education (MOE), Republic of China (Taiwan), with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies

existing.description: The International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program) is a Ministry of Education initiative, run with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies to recruit international students into industry-linked degree programmes in key fields such as STEM, finance and semiconductors. Admitted students receive full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket to Taiwan, initial administrative expense support and a monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000 paid by the partner company, plus paid internships, in exchange for an obligation to work in Taiwan after graduation. Applications are made to individual participating universities, which publish their own deadlines for each Spring and Fall intake, so there is no single programme-wide application date.
eligibility: Must meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.
Must apply to a specific approved INTENSE programme at a participating university, in one of the key industry fields (commonly STEM, finance and semiconductors).
English-taught programmes: CEFR B1 English proficiency required at admission, and TOCFL Level A2 (Listening and Reading) by the end of the first semester of the second academic year.
Chinese-taught programmes: TOCFL Level B1 (Listening and Reading) required.
Some programmes restrict eligible nationalities, for example Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand; others accept students of all nationalities.
Must satisfy the participating university's own programme requirements, including academic performance within the top 50% of the class and a conduct score of not lower than 80 points.
existing.eligibility_summary: International students who meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan and who are recruited by a participating university for an approved INTENSE programme in a key industry field. Nationality targets differ by programme and university, with Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand commonly named, and some programmes open to students of all nationalities. English-taught programmes require CEFR B1 English at admission; Chinese-taught programmes require TOCFL Level B1.
benefits: Full tuition and credit waiver for up to two years.
One-way flight ticket to Taiwan plus initial administrative expense support.
Monthly stipend of at least NT$10,000 for up to two years, paid by the partner company.
Paid summer internships, with allowances not lower than the minimum wage under a bilingual contract.
Priority employment in Taiwan after graduation with a partner company.
coverage: Full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, with universities responsible for tuition subsidies.
Monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000 for up to two years, sponsored by the partner company.
Internship allowances not lower than the Taiwan minimum wage, under a bilingual internship contract.
Priority hiring with partner companies after graduation, at salaries not lower than average.
requirements: Meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.
Meet the participating university's programme-specific academic and language requirements.
Maintain grades in the top 50% of the class and a conduct score of not lower than 80 points, or equivalent to Grade A.
Accept the mandatory internship stage and the employment obligation in Taiwan.
For students already studying in Taiwan at junior or senior undergraduate level, academic performance within the top 50% of the class and a conduct grade of at least 80 or Grade A.
documents: Official transcript of the highest level of degree completed, in Chinese or English (or a certified translation if in neither language)
Proof of language proficiency appropriate to the programme language (CEFR B1 English, or TOCFL as specified)
Passport and, where applicable, Certificate of Entry/Exit Dates from the National Immigration Agency
Self-check for eligibility verification and declaration for international students
Any additional documents required by the individual INTENSE programme
existing.english_requirement: English-taught programmes require CEFR B1 English proficiency at admission, plus TOCFL Level A2 (Listening and Reading) by the end of the first semester of the second academic year. Chinese-taught programmes require TOCFL Level B1 (Listening and Reading).
application_method: Apply directly to the participating university running the specific INTENSE programme through that university's online application portal.
Meet the programme's language and academic requirements; the university handles tuition subsidy, Chinese proficiency verification and employment tracking.
Some programmes run a student nomination step before the national application deadline.
existing.selection_notes: The university's proposal must pass joint review by the Ministry of Education and the relevant ministries before the programme can run, and participating universities must sign contracts with companies to provide student living allowances and internships. Admission is therefore per programme and per intake, with results typically announced in the middle of the year for a September start and in mid-January for a February start.
existing.best_fit: International students from Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand who hold a qualifying degree, meet CEFR B1 English or TOCFL B1 Chinese, and are willing to accept a two-year study-and-internship pathway tied to an obligation to work in Taiwan after graduation.
existing.notes: This is a multi-university national programme, so benefits and deadlines are not uniform. Published packages differ by university: one partner advertises full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket, initial administrative expense support and an NT$10,000 monthly industry-sponsored stipend, while another caps tuition and miscellaneous-fee subsidy at NT$50,000 per semester for up to two years and lists partner-company stipends between NT$10,000 and NT$15,000 depending on the job and Chinese-proficiency requirement. The scheme carries an employment obligation: the stipend duration matches the work-obligation duration and repayment may be requested if the contract is violated. The stored official_source_url and application_link both point to NTU's Overseas Compatriot and Mainland Chinese Students Advising Division, which does not host this programme.
existing.duration: Typically a two-year degree programme of study plus internship, followed by employment in Taiwan.
existing.application_period: Two intakes a year. Spring intake first round runs from early October to late December and second round from early April to late June; the Fall intake mirrors those two rounds. Each participating university publishes its own exact dates, so no single application period applies.
existing.deadline_display: There is no single INTENSE deadline. Each participating university sets its own application window and nomination deadline per intake, and the two intakes do not coincide. Windows published by partner universities for 2027 Spring include 10 September to 12 October 2026 (NCHU), 1 to 22 October 2026 (NCU) and 21 September to 23 October 2026 (KMU), all GMT+8; for 2027 Fall, NTUT publishes a student nomination deadline of 10 March 2027. Applications for several 2027 Spring intakes are open as of 2026-10-04.
existing.program_type: Industry-academia collaboration degree programme (MOE specialised class) with a compulsory employment obligation in Taiwan after graduation

scholarships.title: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: National Taiwan University (NTU), Office of International Affairs

existing.description: The NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship supports current international graduate students at National Taiwan University through a matching-fund structure: NTU waives the student's tuition, while the student's thesis or dissertation supervisor pays a monthly research-assistant salary, with published minimums of TWD 6,000 per month for two years for master's students and TWD 8,000 per month for three years for PhD students, before tax. Applicants must first secure a professor willing to sponsor them and sign the university's word form, and must pass an annual review to keep the award. The published application period is 23 April to 15 May, through NTU's International Degree Current Student System, and roughly half of applicants are awarded.
eligibility: Must be a current international graduate student at NTU.
Overseas Chinese students and Mainland Chinese students are excluded.
Must have a thesis or dissertation supervisor willing to sponsor the award and sign the university's word form.
Must pass the annual review to continue receiving the scholarship.
existing.eligibility_summary: Current international (non-overseas-Chinese, non-Mainland-Chinese) graduate students already enrolled at NTU. Because the award is a matching fund, a graduate student also needs a thesis or dissertation supervisor who is willing to sponsor them and sign the university's word form; scholars must pass an annual review to keep the award.
benefits: Supervisor-paid monthly research-assistant salary, minimum TWD 6,000 per month for master's students (two years) and TWD 8,000 per month for PhD students (three years), before tax.
Renewal for up to two years for master's students and three years for PhD students, subject to annual review.
coverage: Monthly payment from the student's thesis or dissertation supervisor as a research-assistant salary.
Published minimum monthly payment: TWD 6,000 per month for master's students for two years, and TWD 8,000 per month for PhD students for three years, before tax.
requirements: Be a current international graduate student at NTU (overseas Chinese and Mainland Chinese students are excluded).
Secure a sponsoring thesis or dissertation supervisor who will sign the word form and pay the research-assistant salary.
Submit past years' transcripts or an Advisor Evaluation Form.
Submit a recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship and a curriculum vitae.
Pass the annual review to retain the award.
documents: Past years' transcripts, or an Advisor Evaluation Form for graduate students who do not have transcripts
Recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship
Any other documents that strengthen the application, such as award records, proof of outstanding performance or publications
A signed word form from the sponsoring professor
application_method: Submit the application through the International Degree Current Student System during the published application period.
Ask a professor to agree to sponsor the award and have them sign the attached word form, then submit it to the College office.
About half of applicants are awarded the scholarship.
existing.selection_notes: Decision on NTU scholarships is made by the professors of the department to which the applicant belongs. NTU's scholarship FAQ states that about half of applicants receive scholarships. Renewal requires passing review each year.
existing.best_fit: Current international master's or PhD students at NTU who have secured, or can secure, a thesis supervisor willing to sponsor them and commit to a research-assistant salary, and who can pass the annual performance review.
existing.notes: This is not a standalone NTU grant: it is a matching-fund scholarship, so the tuition waiver comes from the university but the monthly income comes from the applicant's own supervisor. Applicants should approach potential supervisors before applying. Do not confuse it with NTU's other awards on the same pages, which have different amounts: the NTU Scholarship for International Degree Student (undergraduate) carries a tuition waiver plus a monthly stipend of NTD 8,000, with tuition fees waived up to NTD 65,000; the NTU Loyalty Award pays NTD 100,000 for master's and NTD 200,000 for PhD places; and the Financial Assistance Grant for International Students is a tuition waiver plus a TWD 6,000 monthly stipend. The stored official_source_url points to NTU's 'Scholarships for Current Students' hub page, whose own content is stale (footer 'Last update : 2024 / 04 / 23') and which does not list this award.
existing.duration: Minimum monthly support for two years for master's students and three years for PhD students, subject to passing an annual review.
existing.application_period: Annual, with a published application period of 23 April to 15 May for existing international degree students at NTU, applying through the International Degree Current Student System.
existing.deadline_display: The published application period on NTU's International Student Services scholarships page is April 23, 2026 - May 15, 2026, submitted through the International Degree Current Student System. The 2026 window has closed; the same window is expected for the next cycle.
existing.program_type: University merit scholarship with a matching-fund structure (university tuition waiver plus a thesis supervisor's research-assistant salary)
